author: DTrim99
body:
Good instinct — it's the same issue as #1125, and the good news is the fix already landed. This record's AGI is $31,428, just over the old $30,000 low-income cap that PolicyEngine was (incorrectly) still applying to the 2022 Vermont child and dependent care credit, so PE was zeroing the credit while TaxAct gave it. That's exactly #1125.

The fix ([PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9263](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/pull/9263), removing the AGI cap that Act 138 repealed) merged on Aug 11, and the run here is on policyengine-us 1.794.2, so it's already included. PE now applies the Vermont CDCC as a refundable credit and matches TaxAct:

| | PE (1.794.2) | TaxAct (IN-111 / IN-112) |
|---|---|---|
| VT income tax before credits | 423.06 | 424 |
| VT CDCC (72% × $780 federal) | 561.60 | 562 |
| VT EITC (38% × federal EITC) | 732.45 | 733 |
| Refundable credits (IN-111 line 25c) | 1,294.05 | 1,295 |
| **State tax / refund** | **−870.99** | **−871 (refund)** |

So they now agree to the dollar (the small gaps are rounding), and the credit is refundable on both sides — the excess over the $424 of tax comes back as a refund. So #1125 wasn't closed prematurely; its fix just needed to reach a release, which it now has (1.794.2). Nothing further needed here — happy to close this as resolved by #1125 unless you're seeing something different on your end.
